# REGIME READ — 2026-09-02

**[FULL-DATA READ]** WebSearch is available, and the option-chain block is present. All seven lenses have live inputs for the second consecutive run.

**Two things dominate this report, and the local news feed reported neither.** First, **the Fed is now expected to RAISE rates on 2026-09-16 — CME FedWatch puts the odds at roughly 66%** after Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole keynote on 2026-08-28. Second, that repricing has triggered a **global bond selloff that has pushed world sovereign yields to their highest since 2008**. The news daemon reports **CLEAR / shock 0.0** and lists three stories about beef markets, AI commentary and Cuban tourism.

**The previous read got the Fed direction wrong, and I am correcting it plainly.** It stated "CME FedWatch has September at 44% and October at 58.3%" and framed those as *cut* odds — it then built the entire NFP playbook on the premise that a weak jobs print would deliver a cut. Multiple sources dated 2026-08-31 and 2026-09-01 (Forbes, CNBC, TechTimes) put the September **hike** probability at 60–68%. The sign was inverted. That error made Lens 3 read **+1** when the correct reading was negative, and it inverted the event playbook: **a strong payroll number on Friday is now the bearish outcome, not the bullish one.**

## Changes Since Previous Read

None of the five Stage-4 triggers I pre-committed to has fired. VIX at **16.35** is the specific reason: Stage 4 requires VIX in the 20–30 band and rising.
- **Total score:** −2 → **−6 (delta −4)**. Unlike last read, **this move is a tape effect, not a data-availability effect.** Data coverage is essentially unchanged run-over-run. Lens 3 Macro flips **+1 → −2** on the hike repricing and the bond selloff; Lens 2 Dealer flow **+1 → 0** as the whole volatility complex lifts. **For the first time in the series, no lens scores positive.**
- **Triggers from previous read:**

Both moved toward the trigger. The ratio closed roughly a quarter of its remaining distance to backwardation in one session.

## Regime Stage Tracker
- **Current Stage:** **3 — Neutral / choppy**, held on discipline and at the edge. VIX **16.35** sits inside the 15–22 band; Stage 4 requires VIX 20–30 *and rising*. The breadth-deterioration half of the Stage-4 description is satisfied, and the Nasdaq-specific gauge is nearly there — **VXN 21.96, up 8.82% in one session** — but the headline gauge is not, and **none of the five Stage-4 triggers I published last read has fired.** I set those thresholds in advance precisely so that a bad session could not talk me into a stage change; I am honouring them.
- **Stage Anchor:** **2026-08-28 — Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote**, which reaffirmed the 2% PCE target against inflation running at **3.7%** and said the Fed may have "work to do." That speech, not the Iran escalation, started the global bond selloff. The **2026-08-31 US–Iran re-escalation** is the amplifier that arrived three days later. Deeper context: the conflict phase began **2026-02-28** with joint US–Israeli strikes on Iran.
- **Position:** Week 1 of a combined rate-repricing and geopolitical-escalation leg, inside a Stage-3 range confirmed across five consecutive reads (08-28, 08-29, 08-31, 09-01, 09-02).
- **Confidence:** **Medium** — upgraded from Low. Four lenses (Macro, Breadth, Cross-asset, Geopolitical) now align bearish, three are neutral, and **none is bullish**. Last read's Low rested on genuine two-sided disagreement between the price of risk and the quantity of risk. That disagreement has largely resolved in one direction: the price of risk is now rising too. The scoring rule gives Medium at four aligned lenses.
- **Bullish trigger (→ Stage 2):** NDX ≥ 30,000 (+3.18%) **with** VXN < 19 — or, more realistically as a first step, September hike odds falling back below 40% on CME FedWatch.
- **Bearish trigger (→ Stage 4):** VIX sustained above 20; **or** VXN > 25; **or** NDX < 28,400 (−2.38%); **or** HY OAS widening through 3.25% from 2.63%; **or** the VIX/VIX3M term ratio rising through 1.00 from 0.891.

## Regime Verdict
A Stage-3 range breaking down from underneath — a hawkish Fed repricing toward a **hike** into a two-decade high in global bond yields, an active US–Iran military exchange lifting crude, and deteriorating participation — with the only remaining support being credit spreads that are still tight and a headline VIX that has not yet caught up to its own Nasdaq counterpart, at **Medium** confidence.

## Diverging Signals

**The tension I described last read has resolved — in the bearish direction.** Last read the split was clean: the *price* of risk (tight credit, deep contango) said calm, while the *quantity* of risk (narrow breadth, geopolitics) said deteriorating. This run, half the calm side defected. The volatility term structure flattened 0.851 → 0.891, VXN jumped 8.82%, VVIX and MOVE rose, and SKEW made a series high. **Only credit is still holding the calm line**, at HY 2.63% / IG 0.80% — and even that widened 3bp. When four of five calm indicators move together toward stress in one session, the reasonable base case is that credit is lagging, not that credit is right.

**Second: the headline VIX is the odd one out, and it is the wrong index for this instrument.** VIX at **16.35** is what keeps the Stage at 3. But **VXN — the Nasdaq-100 gauge, which is the one that actually prices TQQQ premium — is at 21.96 and rose 8.82% in a single session.** The spread between them, 5.61 points, is the widest of the series. NDX fell 1.29% against SPX's 0.71%. **For a Nasdaq-leveraged instrument, the relevant volatility gauge is already behaving like Stage 4 even though the S&P gauge is not.** I hold the stage at 3 because my published trigger says VIX, and I will not move a threshold after the fact — but a reader should know which gauge is speaking about their instrument.

**Third: the news daemon's failure got worse, not better, and this is now a pattern.** Last read it scored **CAUTION / 15.0** and missed a shooting war. This read it scores **CLEAR / 0.0** — the *lowest possible* reading — on a day when the US struck inside Iran, global bond yields hit 2008 highs, NDX fell 1.29%, and futures fell again overnight. Its three top signals are about Tennessee beef markets, an AI opinion column, and Cuban tourism. **The daemon has now been directionally wrong on the single largest driver in two consecutive reads, and its confidence moved the wrong way between them.** A feed that reports 0.0 during a bond crisis and a military escalation is not merely incomplete — a downstream consumer reading `news_shock_score: 0` would conclude the environment is quiet. That is worse than no feed.

**Fourth: a strong jobs number is now the bearish outcome.** With a hike ~66% priced, the reaction function has inverted from what it was through most of this year. A hot NFP on Friday raises hike odds and pressures long-duration tech; a weak one lowers them. Any framework — or any prior read of this series — still assuming "weak jobs = cut = rally" has the sign backwards.

**Fifth: TQQQ's move reconciles this time.** NDX fell **1.29%** and TQQQ fell **3.85%** — a ratio of **2.98×**, essentially exactly the fund's design. Last read flagged an unresolved discrepancy (TQQQ +0.10% against NDX −0.62%); this session shows no such anomaly, which suggests last run's mismatch was a one-off data artefact rather than a systematic feed problem. Recorded so the question can be closed if it does not recur.

## TQQQ Read

- **Momentum: neutral but decisively weakening.** RSI(14) fell from **47.1 to 36.8** in one session — the largest single-session RSI move of the series and the lowest reading of the series. It is still above the 30 line that marks oversold, so this is **not** a washed-out condition offering a mean-reversion tailwind; it is a mid-range indicator travelling fast in one direction. The streak is **1 red**, so there is no multi-day capitulation sequence either. The honest read: momentum has turned negative without yet reaching a level that historically pays a contrarian.

- **Market structure: SIDEWAYS — both tests measured, both fail, but the margins moved.** **DOWNTURN fails on both legs:** spot is **11.23% below** the 4-week high of $77.90 (needs >20%), and VXN at 21.96 is under the ≥25 requirement. **RALLY fails badly:** spot is **1.80% above** the 4-week low of $67.93 (69.15 / 67.93 − 1), against the >30% required. So **SIDEWAYS**. Track the trend across the series: the RALLY margin has collapsed **17.5% → 5.87% → 1.80%**. The classification has not changed for five reads; the instrument's position *within* it has moved from the middle of the range to its floor.

- **Trend: long-horizon cushion intact and thinning; medium-horizon now clearly broken.** Spot is **+13.3% above the 200DMA (~$61.03)** — still a genuine cushion, but down from +17.9% last read; roughly a quarter of that buffer was spent in one session. Against the **50DMA at $71.70**, spot closed **3.55% below** — the **second consecutive close beneath it**, and no longer inside noise the way last read's 0.06% was. The medium-term trend is broken on any ordinary definition.

- **Volatility & premium environment: repricing, and the repricing is the story.** **VXN 21.96, up 8.82% in a single session** — the largest jump of the series — and TQQQ **ATM IV 56.0%**, up from 55.0%. Absolute premium is improving. But the reason it is improving is that risk is being repriced, and every accompanying gauge agrees: **VVIX +5.75%, MOVE +3.40%, SKEW to a series-high 149.23, put/call up to 1.11**, and the term structure flattening **0.851 → 0.891**. The IV/HV reading of **1.44** would ordinarily say premium is rich relative to what the stock has actually been doing — but as set out above, its denominator is unverified this run, and it is being measured against a realized-volatility window that is about to absorb a −3.85% day and, in all likelihood, more. **A rising implied volatility is not a gift to a seller when realized volatility is rising underneath it.**

- **Put-selling context: HOSTILE.** I committed last read to three conditions that would flip this from CAUTIOUS to HOSTILE. With a **~66% hike priced for 2026-09-16**, that mapping is reversed: **a hot number now argues for tightening into a leveraged long-duration index, and a soft number is the relief case.** Historical episodes must be read with that inversion in mind, because both named analogues below occurred under the old, cutting-bias regime.

A three-standard-deviation miss produced a repricing, not a rout — because under the then-prevailing bias, a miss was read as dovish. **Under today's bias the same soft print would be received more favourably still, which is why the asymmetry now sits on the upside surprise.**

This is the left tail when a miss lands together with large negative revisions — a growth scare that overwhelms the rate-relief read.
